topic: Daemon control-plane: get blocking work + coarse locks off the async runtime
notes:
Consolidated from dogfood threads thread-c38e005d + thread-b797e515 (now retired). All citations VALIDATED against beta/blackbox-v2 code this session (commit 9cb5228). Root pattern: blocking work on tokio async workers + coarse locks held across I/O/serialize starves the control/knowledge plane under fleet load. TaskPersister already fixed this for tasks.json; these are the un-fixed siblings.

OPEN / PARTIAL residuals:

A1 [PARTIAL] bro_status / task_status_json holds `task.inner.lock()` across the whole per-event serialize loop. src/orchestration/mod.rs:3367 takes the lock; 3398-3413 iterates inner.events and calls serde_json::to_string per event under it; event-ingest contends on the same lock → /control/status + MCP bro_status can stall under a chatty agent. The cf87a52 56KB size-budget (RECENT_EVENTS_BUDGET_BYTES, mod.rs:3395) bounds worst-case DURATION but the lock is still held across serialization. Fix shape: snapshot under a short lock, serialize off-lock. Adjacent: task_status_json takes inner.lock twice (3366 via task_result_json, then 3367) → eventCount vs recentEvents can be inconsistent.

A2 [OPEN] Tantivy single IndexWriter LockBusy. upsert/delete_knowledge_entry open a FRESH writer per call (src/index/knowledge_docs.rs:116, :135) with no serialization; same at thread_docs.rs:371. Concurrent knowledge/thread mutations race the single-writer lock → "thread index sync failed ... LockBusy" (also collides with the background reindexer per src/server/store_helpers.rs:20-21). Fix shape: one long-lived serialized writer (TaskPersister-style actor) or hand off to the reindex thread via channel; the code NOTEs this exact remedy.

A3 [OPEN] Synchronous full-store fs writes on async workers. notes.rs/threads.rs/knowledge.rs persist via json_store::atomic_write_json_locked (src/json_store.rs:38-64 — File::create + to_writer_pretty + sync_all + rename under a blocking flock), called from MCP handlers (e.g. src/tools/notes.rs:19) that run on tokio workers via the sync Self::run path (src/server/response.rs:67-84). No spawn_blocking. gap-a4e13310 tracks the notes.rs instance specifically (also wants a batch bbox_note_resolve — resolving 40 notes = 40 full-store rewrites under the lock).

A4 [OPEN] MCP cap_response_text (src/server/response.rs:45-59) truncates a >80KB serialized response at a char boundary → still invalid JSON for any tool that builds a large blob via ok_json without upstream size-budgeting. bro_status is now budgeted (A1) so its specific freeze is fixed, but the cap itself remains a JSON-corruption hazard for other large responses. Fix shape: structured/size-aware truncation, or budget at the producer.

These four are one coherent campaign. gap-a4e13310 is the only one currently gap-tracked; consider filing gaps for A1/A2/A4 if pursued.
Picked up in interactive session 2026-06-09: digging into A1-A4 concurrency residuals on beta/blackbox-v2.

Scope broadened by operator: A1-A4 are symptoms; the real work is a holistic concurrency-model redesign. Ran a four-plane code survey (dispatch/harness, index/embed, coordination stores, control plane) on beta/blackbox-v2 @ 9cb5228 and synthesized design/daemon-runtime/concurrency-model.md (lifecycle: proposed; new topic home design/daemon-runtime/ registered in design-corpus.md + PROJECT.md).

Key survey findings beyond A1-A4:
- One flat SharedState (~25 locks), one tokio runtime carrying ALL planes incl. in-process harness loops; 6 ad hoc OS threads; zero spawn_blocking on tool paths — all ~154 sync MCP handlers (incl. bbox_search, refactor planning, reindex) run inline on workers.
- Gen-1 stores (notes/threads/kb/pins/roadmap/projects) do full-store fsync under BOTH the SharedState RwLock write guard and a no-timeout flock, on tokio workers — readers stall behind fsync (worse than the A3 note stated).
- bbox_inbox stacks 5 store read guards; /control/roster locks every task.inner per poll; /tail does per-event team-history file I/O (tail.rs:151).
- Event ingest: inner.events Vec unbounded in memory (50-event cap is persist-only); per-line tee writeln! + allocator/cooldown file I/O on the event path (mod.rs:2644, 2647-2662).
- Documented-but-comment-guarded deadlock cycle at routes.rs:1787-1799 (edge rebuild holds 6 guards across multi-GB scan).
- Reindexer silently SKIPS a pass on LockBusy (reindex.rs:251-253).

Doc proposes: 6-pattern defect taxonomy (P1 blocking-I/O-on-workers, P2 lock-across-I/O, P3 competing single-writer, P4 stacked read guards, P5 unbounded growth, P6 transport truncation); 7 invariants (I1 locks guard memory never I/O; I2 no blocking I/O on workers; I3 one writer per durable resource via owner actors; I4 mutate-fast/persist-async with telemetry vs operator-durable ack classes; I5 bounded memory/queues; I6 control plane reads snapshots; I7 size at producer, transport never corrupts); four-plane target with StorePersister generalization + IndexWriterActor (reindex pass as actor job, small ops interleaved at commit boundaries) + status-snapshot/RosterView publication; second tokio runtime considered and DEFERRED pending tokio-metrics data after Phases 1-3. Migration: Phase 0 instrument + A1/A4, Phase 1 store plane (A3, subsumes gap-a4e13310), Phase 2 index plane (A2), Phase 3 dispatch plane, Phase 4 enforcement.

Next: operator review of the proposed doc, then phase execution under this thread.

PACKET-STORE GROWTH ROOT-CAUSED (follow-up to wire-head finding): the 2,073-file packet store is restart-driven duplication. Boot path restore.rs:130 → restore_runtime_artifacts_from_catalog (routes.rs:1551) re-runs packets.compile() for every active Packet artifact on EVERY daemon start; compile_inner → Self::gen_id() mints a fresh packet-<rand> id + new file each time, no dedupe/supersession by domain or content. 33 active packet artifacts × ~66 daemon restarts (the campaign's own redeploy cadence) = 2,073 files; copies are byte-identical except id/created_at/updated_at. load_latest_by_domain picks newest so behavior stays correct — but the store grows 33 packets/restart, and with the L1 wire-head defect (full-store read per MCP request) every restart makes every subsequent MCP call slower. Compounding feedback loop: deploying concurrency fixes made the wire-head tax heavier. Fix shape: make boot restore idempotent (skip compile when an identical-content packet for that domain/artifact already exists, or supersede prior copies), plus a one-time GC of the duplicates (keep newest per identical-content group). Pairs with the memoization fix — dedupe shrinks the constant, caching removes the per-request scan entirely.
